7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.

19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

## Objective
- The user requested: “Make a joystick.” The project is an existing playable 3D game, and the change adds a more visible, usable on-screen joystick.

## Requirements
- Build the requested change without asking questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) for checks.

## Decisions
- Kept the existing BLOCKRUN game and enhanced its on-screen movement joystick instead of creating a standalone joystick.
- Made touch controls visible across screen sizes; adjusted nearby instructional and objective text to avoid overlap.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the joystick styling and drag range in `index.html`; added active-state feedback and updated movement instructions.
- Verified the module JavaScript with `node --check`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved `screenshots/joystick-desktop.jpg`; browser reported zero errors.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally inspect the screenshot or test joystick interaction at mobile viewport sizes.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: joystick styling, controls, and game.
- `screenshots/joystick-desktop.jpg`: latest visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The development server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; Playwright opened `http://localhost:3002`.

Added a visible, draggable movement joystick to the existing BLOCKRUN game, with active-state feedback and updated movement instructions. I assumed you wanted an on-screen control for the existing game rather than a standalone joystick demo.

Checked the game’s JavaScript syntax and captured `screenshots/joystick-desktop.jpg`. I didn’t verify touch interaction on a mobile device.
